role: Independent source, mathematics and written-pedagogy review; no lesson authorship
binding: Exact lesson content hashes. This is an internal independent review, not an external-provider PR/head approval.

source.inspection: Rendered source page inspected directly; actual authored net layouts and all five source references checked against it.
findings: Exactly five practical construction exercises, one card for each; no omitted subparts.
The source sets no numerical edge length or enlargement factor. All cards preserve a chosen common scale.
Each task requires an enlarged stiff-paper net, cutting and gluing into the named regular solid. Allowances are explicit in 271 and are explained consistently in the remaining cards.

Source net layouts are preserved: four-triangle tetrahedron; four-square cube strip with two leaves at its second square; eight-triangle octahedron; two joined pentagonal flowers; ten-triangle icosahedral strip with two five-triangle fans.

canonicalization: Omit only top-level status and review; recursively sort object keys, preserve array order; Node JSON.stringify UTF-8 SHA256. Aggregate is canonical array in exercise order 271 through 275.

method: Derive all face, hinge, boundary and vertex incidence from actual card coordinates; no author fold metadata imported.
Verify regular unit faces, coplanar CCW orientation, no positive-area overlap, a connected hinge tree, disk Euler count and source-figure hinge-tree topology.
Independently fold the face tree by rigid Rodrigues rotations at the regular-solid normal angles.
Verify closed V/E/F, two faces at every edge, vertex edge/face counts, unit edge lengths, outward supporting planes, convexity and a common circumsphere.
Check all 45 displayed seam pairs against independently folded edge coincidence; every one of 90 boundary edges is used once, with matching midpoint number labels.
Check each illustrative tab lies outside all net faces, attaches to one boundary edge, is nondegenerate and is not counted as a polyhedron face.

findings: Each card teaches net construction, a common scale, uncut folds, allowances, dry fitting, gluing and final inspection.
Each seam is individually reachable, and pair numbers are distinguished from a required gluing order.
The dodecahedron construction uses five equal central angles of 72 degrees; the triangle constructions use two equal-radius arcs. The source imposes no compass-and-straightedge-only restriction.
All five completion prompts preserve manual assessment of a physical model or its photographs. Opening steps does not certify completion.
Closed regular-solid examples are linked through existing theory; the main scene is correctly presented as a flat paper net.
Correct face, edge, vertex and per-vertex incidence counts support the final model checks; tabs are not additional faces.

resolvedFindings.resolution: Author corrected the Russian plural agreement for seven and five seam pairs before final binding.
Author corrected the 275 step-8 edge-count explanation to «20 граней по 3 стороны» before final binding.

limitations: This record does not claim browser screenshot or responsive-layout inspection; that review is separate.
Ideal rigid-face closure is verified; no physical paper model, continuous collision-free folding path, glue performance or real-pupil learning pilot was tested.
No paid external-provider review is claimed.
Later material lesson or oracle changes require renewed review; status/review-only changes do not alter the canonical lesson binding.
